name: Travel and Leisure

mofsl_2qfy27.headline: Mixed 2QFY27 performance; growth outlook remains constructive (page heading confirmed as 'TRAVEL & LEISURE'; the section covers online travel only, there is no separate Hotels, Aviation or amusement park section in the compendium)
mofsl_2qfy27.read: The Travel & Leisure page covers TBO Tek, Ixigo and Yatra: aggregate revenue grew 16.4% YoY (41.8% in 1QFY27), EBITDA 60.2%, EBITDA margin 12.4% and PAT 25.0%. TBO Tek's organic revenue grew 14% on 22% GTV growth with EBITDA margin 16.7% (above estimates); Ixigo revenue grew 13% on 22% GTV growth (hotel GTV ~26x YoY) with EBITDA margin 5.6%, below estimates; Yatra revenue was INR2,136m and EBITDA INR108m, below estimates. Hotels, airlines and parks appear only through the Nifty results table (page 9): IndiGo sales INR234b (+26% YoY, in line), EBITDA INR22b (+156% YoY, 16% below estimates) and a PAT loss of INR21b; Indian Hotels is on MOFSL's top-ideas list. Guidance: TBO expects improving agent productivity, a favourable Hotels and Ancillary mix and Classic Vacations synergies; Ixigo is scaling Hotels and Buses with near-term margin pressure; Yatra expects a stronger 2HFY27 on MICE, corporate travel and efficiencies. MOFSL keeps BUY on TBO Tek, Neutral on Ixigo and downgrades Yatra to Neutral.

unit_economics: Hotels: room revenue = keys x days x occupancy x ARR (RevPAR = occupancy x ARR) with 55-60% fixed cost, so ARR growth flows near 100% to EBITDA. Airlines: operating spread = PRASK - cost per ASK (fuel, ownership, airport, staff). Parks: revenue = footfall x (ticket price + non-ticket spend) on a mostly fixed cost base. Online travel: revenue = GTV x take rate.

price_drivers.why: ARR growth drops through at ~100% to EBITDA and occupancy at ~55-60%; Indian Hotels standalone occupancy of 82% in Q2FY27 means further growth must come from ARR.

price_drivers.driver: Airline PRASK versus fuel (ATF) and USD/INR
price_drivers.why: IndiGo 2QFY27 EBITDA of INR22b was 16% below estimates and PAT was a INR21b loss; fuel and FX translation on dollar lease liabilities swing quarterly profit more than traffic does.

price_drivers.driver: Online travel GTV growth and take rate
price_drivers.why: TBO Tek GTV +22% and Ixigo GTV +22% drove 13-14% revenue growth; margin outcomes diverged (TBO 16.7% vs Ixigo 5.6%) on investment in Hotels and AI.

price_drivers.driver: Hotel supply additions in key cities and keys pipeline
price_drivers.why: Branded pipeline of ~161k rooms against ~9% supply growth caps occupancy and rate in cities where supply lands.

price_drivers.driver: Park footfall and weather or event shocks
price_drivers.why: Park cost is largely fixed, so a 6% footfall drop moved Wonderla margin from 47.4% to 32.1%; peak-day weather or a health advisory can remove 30-40% of a day's visitors.

kpis.name: Hotel occupancy, ARR and RevPAR (comparable basis)
kpis.definition: Occupancy, average room rate and RevPAR on the company's like-for-like hotel set, with growth split into rate and occupancy.
kpis.formula: RevPAR = occupancy x ARR; room revenue = average keys x days x RevPAR
kpis.why_it_moves_price: RevPAR growth compounds through 55-60% fixed costs: Indian Hotels standalone RevPAR rose 28% to Rs13,860 in Q2FY27 (partly the BRICS summit), and listed hotels trade at 15-25x FY28E EV/EBITDA on the view that rate growth persists above 4-5% cost inflation.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'RevPAR', 'ARR' and 'occupancy' for INDHOTEL, CHALET, LEMONTREE and others (decks and transcripts in the library); get_financials for revenue and EBITDA; broker results notes (Jefferies CoStar and HVS monthly city data).
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus on RevPAR; get_consensus_estimates gives Sales, EBITDA and EPS; broker models in the library and monthly CoStar and HVS industry data via broker notes; management commentary in transcripts.
kpis.traps: Three industry series (Hotelivate, HVS Anarock, CoStar) are not comparable; company LFL cut-offs move (IHCL); occupancy bases exclude out-of-order rooms (Chalet); one-off event revenue (BRICS) and acquisitions inflate growth.

kpis.name: Airline PRASK, yield and load factor
kpis.definition: Passenger revenue per available seat km = yield x passenger load factor, with fuel recapture measured as the change in PRASK over the change in fuel per ASK.
kpis.formula: PRASK = yield x PLF; fuel recapture = delta PRASK / delta fuel per ASK
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Fares set the spread: IndiGo's 1QFY27 PRASK +~19.5% covered only ~74% of an ~80% rise in fuel per ASK, so weak fare recapture or fare caps (a 5% yield cut is ~10% of EBITDA per Nomura) drive the stock more than traffic.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'yield', 'PRASK', 'RASK' and 'PLF' for INDIGO (indexed in Airavat); transcripts via get_qa; DGCA monthly traffic and share from broker notes; get_financials for revenue.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for INDIGO Sales, EBITDA and EPS; no consensus for PRASK; company PRASK and capacity guidance in transcripts; broker models in the library.
kpis.traps: Company RASK includes other income and hedge gains; OEM compensation sits in revenue; temporary fare caps; PRASK vs yield definitions differ across brokers.

kpis.name: Park footfall, ATP and non-ticket spend per head
kpis.definition: Ticketed park entries, average ticket price (net of GST) and spend on F&B and merchandise per visitor, split between like-for-like parks and new parks.
kpis.formula: ARPU = park revenue / footfall; ATP = entry-fee revenue / footfall
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Footfall drives operating leverage on a fixed cost base; Wonderla FY26 ATP was Rs1,061 and mature-park footfall fell 2-7% in FY26 before recovering 6-11% in Q1FY27, so the market pays for LFL footfall, not new-park announcements.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metrics 'footfall', 'ATP' and 'ARPU' for WONDERLA and IMAGICAA (Imagicaa is indexed in the vector DB); transcripts via search_research; get_financials for revenue.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for Sales and EBITDA (thin coverage); no consensus on footfall; broker notes in the library (Ambit, ICICI Direct, I-Sec, Monarch); management guidance in transcripts.
kpis.traps: Footfall definition (complimentary and resort guests); Imagicaa has multiple ARPU definitions and perimeter changes; weather, school calendars and advisories distort quarters.

kpis.name: Online travel GTV growth and take rate
kpis.definition: Gross travel value (bookings) growth by air, hotels, buses and corporate travel, with revenue as a percentage of GTV.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: GTV growth sets revenue and take rate sets margin: TBO Tek (GTV +22%, 16.7% EBITDA margin) rated BUY while Ixigo (GTV +22%, 5.6% margin) and Yatra (revenue INR2,136m, miss) were rated Neutral, since investors pay for operating leverage not bookings.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metrics 'GTV' and 'take rate' for IXIGO (indexed in Airavat) and the TBOTEK and YATRA decks in the library; get_financials for revenue and EBITDA; transcripts via search_research.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for Sales, EBITDA and EPS; GTV guidance in transcripts; broker models (MOFSL, Jefferies) in the library.
kpis.traps: Revenue is net or gross by business model; GTV definitions differ; acquisitions (Classic Vacations); organic vs reported growth.

kpis.name: Keys pipeline, signings and management fee income
kpis.definition: Owned, leased and managed keys, signings versus openings, capital-light share of pipeline and management fee income per managed key.
kpis.formula: fee per managed key = management fee income / average managed keys
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Fee income carries 65-80% margin and is valued at 35-50x EBITDA, so brand-led names such as INDHOTEL (pipeline >90% capital-light) trade at 25x FY28E against 15-17x for owners.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'keys', 'signings' and 'pipeline' for INDHOTEL, LEMONTREE, CHALET; transcripts; get_financials for fee revenue.
kpis.estimate_source: Management guidance on signings and openings in transcripts; broker models in the library; no consensus.
kpis.traps: Acquired conversions counted as openings (IHCL's Clarks hotels); signings slip 8-16 quarters to opening; midscale signings earn a fraction of luxury fees per key.

kpis.name: Core CASK ex-fuel ex-FX and ownership cost
kpis.definition: Total expenses excluding fuel, FX loss and exceptional items per ASK, with aircraft ownership cost per ASK.
kpis.formula: (total expenses - fuel - FX loss - exceptionals) / ASK
kpis.why_it_moves_price: The cost lead over rivals is the moat: IndiGo's FY26 CASK ex-fuel ex-FX rose 3.8% against guidance that was raised twice, and cost guidance drift on crew rules, INR and damp leases feeds straight into estimates.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation filters 'CASK' and 'ownership cost' for INDIGO; get_financials expense lines; transcripts for guidance.
kpis.estimate_source: Management CASK guidance in transcripts; broker models in the library; no consensus.
kpis.traps: Company version subtracts finance income; ownership shifts move maintenance below EBITDAR; brokers use different cost bases.

kpis.name: ATF price, fuel per ASK and USD/INR translation
kpis.definition: Jet fuel cost per ASK against the ATF index and Singapore jet crack, and the mark-to-market FX loss on dollar lease liabilities.
kpis.formula: fuel per ASK = fuel cost / ASK; FX MTM = net USD exposure x change in closing rate
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Fuel is 28-35% of revenue in a normal year and 44% in a shock; IndiGo's FY26 FX loss was Rs89.8bn, mostly non-cash lease translation, so ATF and USD/INR together explain most of the EBITDA miss and the PAT loss in 2Q.
kpis.history_source: get_commodity_prices for crude, ATF-linked benchmarks and INR:USD; get_financials for fuel and FX lines; get_investor_presentation for fuel per ASK.
kpis.estimate_source: Forward crude and INR from get_commodity_prices and Kotak assumptions via get_commodity_assumptions; management hedging commentary in transcripts; no consensus on fuel per ASK.
kpis.traps: Published ATF index differs from effective price paid (international uplift, private suppliers); OMC cap regimes; hedge gains sit in other income.

kpis.name: Park EBITDA margin (ex other income) and new-park maturity
kpis.definition: EBITDA excluding other income and exceptionals over revenue from operations, with new-park margin by months open.
kpis.formula: (revenue - operating costs) / revenue, ex other income
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Margin swung 47.4% to 32.1% on a 6% footfall fall at Wonderla; management claims new parks reach 40-45% by years 3-4, so cohort evidence (Chennai ~48% in Q1FY27 against Bhubaneswar's missed footfall guides) sets valuation of the pipeline.
kpis.history_source: get_financials for WONDERLA and IMAGICAA; get_investor_presentation for park EBITDA snippets; transcripts for new-park margin.
kpis.estimate_source: Management margin commentary in transcripts; broker models; get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA only.
kpis.traps: Company EBITDA bases flip between including and excluding other income; treasury income is a large share of PBT; one-offs (labour code, deferred tax credits).

kpis.name: Online travel EBITDA margin and operating leverage
kpis.definition: EBITDA over revenue (or over GTV) for online travel platforms, with investment in hotels, buses and AI shown separately.
kpis.formula: EBITDA / revenue; EBITDA as % of GTV
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Margins separate the group: TBO Tek 16.7% (above MOFSL estimates), Ixigo 5.6% (below, on hotel and AI investment) and Yatra EBITDA of INR108m (below); operating leverage guidance (TBO) is rewarded.
kpis.history_source: get_financials for IXIGO, TBOTEK, YATRA; get_investor_presentation filter 'EBITDA margin'; transcripts for investment plans.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA and EPS; management margin commentary in transcripts; broker models.
kpis.traps: Gross vs net revenue recognition; ESOP costs; one-time integration costs after acquisitions.

macro_inputs.series: ATF (jet fuel) price, Singapore jet crack and Brent crude
macro_inputs.source: Airavat get_commodity_prices for crude and ATF-linked series; get_commodity_assumptions for Kotak forward assumptions
macro_inputs.why: Fuel is the largest airline cost; PRASK recapture lags by about a quarter
FX loss on dollar leases for airlines; foreign-guest revenue for luxury hotels

macro_inputs.series: Domestic and international air passengers (DGCA, MoCA); foreign tourist arrivals
macro_inputs.source: DGCA monthly files via broker notes in the library
macro_inputs.why: Demand and fare lead for airlines, OTAs and luxury hotels

macro_inputs.series: Industry RevPAR by city (CoStar, HVS), wedding dates, branded supply and pipeline
macro_inputs.source: Jefferies, Nomura and Investec sector notes in the library
macro_inputs.why: Hotel RevPAR true-up and supply risk in the company's cities

macro_inputs.series: Weather and school calendars; state health advisories
macro_inputs.source: IMD and company transcripts via search_research
macro_inputs.why: Park footfall in Q1 and Q3 peaks

valuation_anchor: Hotels on forward EV/EBITDA on house operating EBITDA with SOTP (fees at a higher multiple, annuity at cap rate); airlines on EV/EBITDAR with lease-inclusive net debt and P/E on core PAT; parks on per-park DCF and EV/EBITDA; online travel on EV/EBITDA and P/E.
watch_next_quarter: Per MOFSL, TBO Tek expects sustained operating leverage, Ixigo remains focused on scaling Hotels and Buses (limiting near-term profitability) and Yatra anticipates a stronger 2HFY27 on MICE and corporate travel: watch GTV growth and margins at each, and for hotels, airlines and parks, which MOFSL's compendium does not cover separately, IndiGo's fuel recapture after its 2QFY27 EBITDA miss.
